content.tex: The cylinder turns clockwise about its axis of symmetry. The pencil does not move but draws a line on the paper. The cylinder stops turning at the end of one full turn.

This diagram shows the paper when it is unwrapped from the cylinder. \(AB\) is shown at the top and bottom of the rectangle because \(AB\) is where the two long edges meet on the cylinder. The length of the line drawn by the pencil is shown by the line \(AA\) in the rectangle.
Explain why the length of the line drawn by the pencil is 31.4cm, correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.text: A new piece of paper is wrapped around the cylinder in the same way. The cylinder turns clockwise about its axis of symmetry. AB rotates at a speed of 2 cm /s as shown by the curved arrow. The pencil moves along the horizontal track at a speed of 2 cm /s. After one complete turn of the cylinder the pencil is at X, a point on AB. The paper is unwrapped from the cylinder. On the unwrapped paper the curved line appears as a straight line. The curved line on the cylinder is called a helix. The distance along AB to where the pencil meets AB again is called the pitch of the helix.

content.tex: A new piece of paper is wrapped around the cylinder in the same way.
The cylinder turns clockwise about its axis of symmetry. \(AB\) rotates at a speed of 2cm/s as shown by the curved arrow. The pencil moves along the horizontal track at a speed of 2cm/s.
After one complete turn of the cylinder the pencil is at X, a point on AB.
The paper is unwrapped from the cylinder. On the unwrapped paper the curved line appears as a straight line.
The curved line on the cylinder is called a helix.
The distance along \(AB\) to where the pencil meets \(AB\) again is called the pitch of the helix.
